item.title: Apate sends AI agents undercover to get scammed so they can gather fraud intelligence
item.dc:creator: Ram Iyer
item.description: Most companies use AI agents to ship products faster or speed up workflows. Apate.ai sends them undercover to get scammed.

item.title: Mosqitter is turning its mosquito traps into an AI-powered surveillance network
item.dc:creator: Kate Park
item.description: Mosqitter is turning its mosquito-trapping hardware into an AI-powered surveillance network designed to identify species, monitor populations, and provide earlier warnings of mosquito-borne disease risks.

item.title: Prismm helps banks keep inherited money in-house
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: With Prismm, account holders can give designated family members access to their accounts and documents ahead of time.

item.title: Deezer will soon let you filter out AI-generated music
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Deezer said that the new toggle will be rolled out by the end of the year.

item.title: Save 50% on your TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 ticket and join the last 2 days in San Francisco’s Moscone West
item.dc:creator: TechCrunch Events
item.description: Get a 50% discount on the last two days of TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, October 14-15, in San Francisco. Register now and join the rest of the startup ecosystem. Today, it's all about physical and software AI.

item.title: Zenzap raises $44M for its AI chat app that aims to replace WhatsApp in the workplace
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Zenzap is used by organizations including Starbucks and Taco Bell.

item.title: Floqer’s AI agents research sales prospects so teams don’t have to
item.dc:creator: Lauren Forristal
item.description: The problem Floqer is trying to solve is familiar to anyone who has worked in sales or revenue operations.

item.title: Netflix to lay off 1,000 staff amid intensifying competition for user attention
item.dc:creator: Ram Iyer
item.description: Netflix said most of the cuts would affect its product, tech, legal, and human resources departments.

item.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: Day 2
item.dc:creator: TechCrunch Events
item.description: Day 2 at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, full of all themes across AI, investor-only session, more roundtables, and more. Register to save 50% on your pass.

item.title: NTangible bets it can predict how athletes will perform under pressure
item.dc:creator: Amanda Silberling
item.description: NTangible is building an analytics platform for collegiate sports organizations and other clubs to measure an athlete's "clutch" factor.

item.title: Scimplify raises $25M to challenge China’s grip on critical materials with AI
item.dc:creator: Jagmeet Singh
item.description: Scimplify's annualized revenue run rate has tripled to $200 million as it eyes U.S. expansion.

item.title: Justice Department says North Koreans have infiltrated dozens of US companies
item.dc:creator: Zack Whittaker
item.description: U.S. authorities warn that sanctioned hackers are increasingly targeting Americans to act as facilitators between breached U.S. companies and Pyongyang.

item.title: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: Max Hodak, the former president and co-founder of Neuralink, detailed onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt how his company's work with PRIMA is part of its path toward a novel brain-computer interface (BCI).

item.title: Cerebras CEO says we’re nearing a future where everyone has a personal AI assistant at home
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman predicts a future where personal AI assistants become as commonplace as household appliances, running partly on local devices and partly in the cloud.

item.title: Industrial Next wants factory robots to switch tasks in minutes, not weeks
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: Industrial Next helps manufacturers automate complex, delicate tasks that have traditionally required human labor.

item.title: Cerebras CEO pushes back on AI doomsday warnings
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman has a message for AI leaders spreading doomsday warnings: Maybe stop talking? At TechCrunch Disrupt, he argued that the industry's focus on AI's risks is drowning out its potential benefits.

item.title: Helix Carbon says it can make iron cheaper by recycling blast furnace pollution
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant
item.description: The steel industry is a big polluter, but Helix Carbon can upcycle pollution from blast furnaces to drive down emissions and improve margins.

item.title: FBI arrests OpenAI employee accused of planting hidden recording device in conference room
item.dc:creator: Zack Whittaker
item.description: It's not clear exactly for what purpose the recording device was used, but FBI director Kash Patel said the scheme was to "capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology."

item.title: Judge orders OpenAI to turn over hiring records in Apple trade secrets case
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: A federal judge ruled that Apple can access OpenAI's interview materials involving former Apple employees, as well as private messages and testimony from key figures in the case.

item.title: Cambridge Heavy Industries has been quietly building a desktop fusion device
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant
item.description: Fusion power startup Cambridge Heavy Industries is building a small, laser-powered fusion device to fuel the coming wave of fusion power plants.
